name: The Tome of Divinity

angles.text: For a paladin, the Tome of Divinity sets out the moral heart of the calling: compassion and patience matter as much as readiness for combat.
Stormwind’s paladins form the Alliance’s spiritual and martial backbone. They anchor the realm’s defense in moral integrity and humble service to ordinary citizens.
For Stormwind’s humans, studying the holy tome is a sacred rite of passage that reinforces civic duty and devotion to the Holy Light.

faq.answer: Paladins in Stormwind study the Tome of Divinity as a sacred guide to their calling. Its teachings reject godhood and personal glory, urging them to reflect the Holy Light through goodness, compassion, and patience.
faq.q: What is the Tome of Divinity?

faq.answer: Duthorian Rall is a paladin leader in Stormwind who guides young paladins’ study of the Tome of Divinity. He oversees their spiritual and martial trials, testing their resolve through practical service to the kingdom and its people.

The Tome of Divinity teaches that compassion, patience, and bravery matter as much to a holy warrior as skill in combat. Paladins must smite wickedness, but their nobility lies in aiding the vulnerable and reflecting the Light’s benevolence.
faq.q: What virtues does the Tome of Divinity emphasize?

faq.answer: Duthorian Rall tests initiates to see whether they have truly taken the Tome of Divinity’s teachings to heart. They must show sound judgment and patience in serving the less fortunate, proving their devotion rests on service rather than pride.
faq.q: Why does Duthorian Rall test aspiring paladins?

faq.answer: No. The Tome of Divinity rejects the pursuit of godhood and teaches paladins to seek goodness in every deed. The Light grants them strength to protect and support others, not to place themselves above fellow mortals.
faq.q: Does the Tome of Divinity teach paladins to seek godhood?

aliases: where is the tome of divinity quest
where to turn in tome of divinity
faq.answer: The trials take place in the human kingdom of Stormwind. Initiates study the sacred teachings and report to Duthorian Rall in the city, then undertake trials of charity, patience, and valor through the streets and surrounding lands.
faq.q: Where does this quest take place?

faq.answer: Patience shows that a holy warrior is disciplined, humble, and sound of mind. Serving the downtrodden often means taking on humble, difficult, or unglamorous tasks, which call for emotional steadfastness and genuine empathy as well as courage in battle.
faq.q: Why is patience so important for a paladin of the Light?

sections.body: The Tome of Divinity’s sacred texts teach paladin initiates what it means to serve the Light. Divinity means neither seeking godhood nor claiming rule over others. Instead, champions reflect the Light’s grace through pure intent and goodness in every deed. Paladins take up arms against evil, but strength without moral purpose means little. Their true distinction lies in how they treat ordinary people across Azeroth, keeping power bound to righteousness and humility.
sections.title: The Nature of Divinity

sections.body:
Scripture is only the beginning of a paladin’s service. After an initiate studies the Tome of Divinity, Duthorian Rall in Stormwind tests whether its lessons have taken root in the candidate’s heart and mind. The Light asks for more than the slaying of beasts. It calls for patience, bravery, and understanding.

In the city and the surrounding lands, people suffer and humble tasks go without glory. By aiding the less fortunate and comforting those in despair, an initiate proves they have the sound mind and selfless spirit to bear the Light’s blessings responsibly.
sections.title: Trials of Compassion and Patience

summary: In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides the first steps of paladin training. Its teachings call champions of the Holy Light to humility, compassion, and patience, not godhood or strength alone.
